correctness.rationale: For the finite open chain with positive alternating a,b, T* T has diagonal a²+b² and off-diagonal ab. The orthonormal sine vectors give simple positive singular values E_l, paired eigenvectors (Tv_l/E_l,±v_l)/√2, and a single A-only vector with w_(x+1)=−(a/b)w_x. The span of clean eigenvectors zero on all lossy sites reduces both H and the loss matrix. An eigenstate on its orthogonal complement cannot have real eigenvalue under K: taking the imaginary part forces it to vanish at every monitored site, making it a clean dark eigenstate. Thus the complement decays even with Jordan blocks, and total survival is the dark-projector trace. For the B monitors the common sine-node indices are l=tn/g by Bézout; the sine-square sum is zero when g divides x and g/n otherwise, giving the asserted weights and dimension. The A-input finite sum follows from the left components and the normalized zero mode. A single A absorber sees the zero mode everywhere; consecutive sine factors cannot both vanish, so a nonzero pair survives exactly at the stated positive ratios. Endpoints see all eigenvectors. At n=6,j=2 the positive roots of b/a=−2 cos(πl/6) are 1 and √3, with one pair each. The example correctly asserts √3 is locally isolated, not that it is the only resonance. The maximally mixed formula follows from the projector trace. Frozen verification files were inspected, not executed.
